artists.biography:
Yazoo (also known as Yaz in the United States) is a British synthpop duo from Basildon, Essex. It had a number of Top 10 hits in the UK charts in the early 1980s. Formed in late 1981 by former Depeche Mode songwriter Vince Clarke (synthesizer) and Alison Moyet (vocals), Yazoo was signed to Mute Records in the United Kingdom and (as "Yaz") to Sire Records in the United States.
 
Yazoo's debut single "Only You" backed with "Situation", was released on 15 March 1982 and rose to number two in the UK charts. Yazoo released two successful studio albums, Upstairs at Eric's in 1982 and You and Me Both in 1983. Shortly after, Moyet and Clarke decided to break up. Moyet pursued a solo career while Clarke went on to form Erasure, another synth pop duo. Yazoo reunited in 2008 with a tour in Europe and the United States and the release of a four-disc box set.
 
Though the band's initial run was short-lived, Yazoo continues to influence and inspire many of today's bands, including LCD Soundsystem, Shiny Toy Guns, Blaqk Audio, Hercules and Love Affair, La Roux and Gil Mantera's Party Dream.

perplexity.description:
Released in August 1982 on Mute Records, Upstairs at Eric's is the debut album by English synth-pop duo Yazoo, consisting of Vince Clarke and Alison Moyet. The album is a landmark in electronic pop, blending Clarke’s minimalist, melodic synth arrangements with Moyet’s powerful, soulful vocals. Its sound is defined by stark, atmospheric synthesizers, crisp drum machines, and emotionally resonant songwriting, exemplified by the iconic singles “Only You” and “Don’t Go.” The title references Blackwing Studios in London, where the album was recorded on the first floor with engineer Eric Radcliffe.

Upstairs at Eric's stands as Yazoo’s most influential and critically acclaimed work, reaching number two on the UK Albums Chart and earning recognition as one of the finest synth-pop albums of the 1980s. It is widely regarded as the duo’s creative peak, preceding their second and final studio album, You and Me Both (1983). Over the years, the album has been included in major retrospectives, such as Rolling Stone’s list of the 100 Best Debut Albums of All Time and Paste’s ranking of the greatest synth-pop albums. Its enduring legacy lies in its innovative fusion of electronic production and emotive pop songcraft.
